statement: Guitar-TECHS provides redistributable electric-guitar DI, amplified and room recordings with MIDI under CC BY 4.0.
P1 single-note reference spread supports a median 21-band RMS regression threshold of 24.538530602719486 dB.
Observed P1 attack range is 8.208333333333334–31.541666666666668 ms under the frozen onset algorithm.
A causal dual-polarisation modal/contact architecture can span the frozen construction and playing controls with finite output.
The spike achieves median band RMS 17.95823076278605 dB against the calibration references.
Construction parameters have coupled physical effects; material names alone cannot guarantee reproduction of an arbitrary instrument.
JUCE 8 supports VST3 and APVTS-based plug-in state on the declared desktop platforms.
Versioned GitHub runner labels cover the declared desktop and ARM64 Linux jobs.

claim: Neck-joint construction has measured but inconsistent effects on sustain: one guitar converted neck-through -> bolt-on -> set neck measured longest sustain as bolt-on while listeners heard no sustain difference (Mottola 2007); a nine-guitar study (3 screwed, 3 glued, 3 neck-through) reportedly found joint-related differences in fundamental decay but few tonal differences and almost none in sustain (Paté et al.; read only through a secondary write-up); a magazine measurement found equal decay times for glued and bolt-on (via Zollner). No source supports a consistent rule such as 'bolt-on is snappier, neck-through sustains longer'. Supersedes C-028.
